published_implementation.historical_relation: First-party repository-history witness whose enactment merge is an ancestor of the canonical review revision. It is descriptive evidence, not an independently reproduced numeric benchmark run.

observations.result_form: immutable policy-change, enactment, executable-return and lineage-persistence witness
observations.policy_change_commit_message: Clarify Cyber Pro evidence without internal veto
observations.enactment_pr_title: Integrate selected issue sprint across runtime and UI
observations.authority_issue: who holds ultimate internal review and configuration authority in Cyber Pro, including whether independent review evidence can veto action and whether context/safety settings remain owner-only
decision_chain: Cyber Pro ultimate internal review/configuration authority is treated as an identity/ultimate-policy matter in canonical Ouroboros
ouroboros-agent authors constitutional and runtime changes for the owner-selected issue sprint
repository owner razzant merges PR #855 into the canonical repository
BIBLE.md changes the constitutional rule so Cyber Pro review evidence remains factual but cannot become an internal veto or permission request
runtime_mode_policy.py and config.py implement the changed authority boundary in executable first-party code
tests/test_review_cyber_authority.py executes the policy distinction between pro and cyber_pro while preserving review facts
the merge commit remains an ancestor of the later canonical review revision and the changed runtime policy remains present there
executable_effects: Cyber Pro receives unrestricted internal action authority while independent review findings remain preserved as evidence
context-mode and safety-mode lowering remain owner-only outside Cyber Pro but are authorable in Cyber Pro
review-gate tests demonstrate Cyber Pro can continue or commit after failed/pending review without relabeling or discarding the review evidence
observations.provenance_note: This is a descriptive first-party repository-history observation, not an independently reproduced benchmark run. The parent-governed attribution is based on the PR explicitly describing owner-selected work and GitHub recording repository owner razzant as the merger. The observation does not establish that autonomous Cyber Pro independently selected this constitutional change.
